newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK's Hang Seng closes lower, snapping record run.
newsitem.headline: HK's Hang Seng closes lower, snapping record run.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index broke its record run on Tuesday with a lower close as investors took profits ahead of U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's testimony to the Senate banking committee.
After four straight record closes, the blue-chip index finished down 135.45 points, or 0.98 percent, at 13,732.79. Turnover was HK$9.45 billion against HK$11.35 billion on Monday.

"I think people are cautious about tonight's speech by Alan Greenspan. A month ago there was turbulent trading right after his speech," said Patrick Chia, research director at China Everbright Research.
Comments made by Greenspan in December prompted a bout of interest rate jitters, setting off a drop of more than 600 points in the Hang Seng during one session.
The Fed chairman is due to testify on the state of the U.S. economy later on Tuesday.
"The market is sort of at pretty high levels so anything he says will be analysed carefully," said Richard Verin, head of equities trading CS First Boston.
Banking stocks took the biggest hit after leading the market to its recent record highs. Shares in HSBC Holdings fell HK$3.50 to HK$180.50 and Hang Seng Bank dropped HK$1.75 to HK$94.00.
"Last week's rally was almost exclusively the banking sector, so what you are seeing now is just a bit of profit-taking," said Verin.
He said a number of share placements had also soaked up liquidity in the market. "There has been a lot of paper issued. There is a lot to digest," he said.
Failed attempts to get through 14,000 points signalled that the market was in for a period of consolidation, analysts said.
Chia said he expected a range of 13,700 to 14,000 points for the rest of the week.
"I think it depends a little bit on the U.S. and how it reacts to what happens tonight, and you have got to wait and look for what sector is going to assume leadership," said Verin.
"There seems to be a bit of focus on the conglomerates. You need that sector to take leadership."
Shares in Hutchison Whampoa were among the few gainers in the Hang Seng Index. The stock rose HK$1.00 to HK$63.25.
Shares in Television Broadcasts Ltd (TVB) hit a 12-month high at HK$34.80 before closing up HK$1.70 at HK$34.50.
January Hang Seng Index futures fell 115 points to 13,720.
